US energy storage installed a record 20.2 GWh in calendar Q2 2026 (17.9-18.0 GWh utility-scale, 1.8 GWh commercial/industrial), 30.8 GWh in H1, and SEIA/Benchmark RAISED the full-year 2026 forecast to 71 GWh versus 59 GWh installed in 2025 - published 2026-09-01, twelve weeks after ABM last spoke, and covering the two months (May, June) that sit inside ABM's fiscal Q3.
why_not_priced: ABM's Technical Solutions grew 27.2% in Q2 FY26 explicitly on battery energy storage, and the entire FY26 adjusted-EPS guide rests on management's claim that 'volume will ramp meaningfully in ATS' in the back half - the single most doubted line in the guide, because ATS margin was diluted in Q2 by equipment-heavy BESS work. The datapoint that validates it sits in solar/storage trade press a week before the print, on a $2.8bn company with only three published estimates; no ABM preview carries it. If the market had made the connection, ABM would not be sitting 4.68% below its 52-week high with 15.1% annualised realised vol into a print where its fastest-growing segment's end market just set an all-time quarterly record and had its annual outlook raised 20%. Note this also refutes the Wood Mackenzie call (published 2025-07-01) that US grid-scale BESS would contract 29% in 2026 on FEOC and tariff constraints, which is the version of this story that was current when ABM guided.

text: CBRE's Q2 2026 US office report (2026-07-29) shows national vacancy falling 30bp to 18.3% - 'the largest quarterly decline since 2015' - net absorption of 12.6m sq ft, nearly double the prior quarter and a ninth straight positive quarter, leasing +16% y/y, with CBRE projecting 2026 annual leasing to surpass the 2022 record; San Francisco, the exact market ABM's CEO singled out on 2026-06-05 as having vacancy 'probably 2 or 3x worse than New York City', posted +963,980 sq ft of net absorption in the quarter.
why_not_priced: Business & Industry is ~44% of ABM revenue ($1,015.8m of $2,290.0m in Q2) and was flat y/y, which management attributed to UK and West Coast client exits driven by CRE weakness. The office inflection is fully priced in office REITs, which are the constituency that reads CBRE Figures; it is not priced in a janitorial contractor covered by three analysts, because the transmission runs through re-scoping, occupancy-linked hours and win rates rather than through any line an ABM preview models. If it were priced you would see ABM bid into the print rather than -3.07% over 20 days, and you would see at least one of the three estimates moving after 2026-07-29. Sized small deliberately: janitorial scope lags leasing by several quarters, and near-term reported B&I is dominated by the disclosed Transport for London exit worth ~300bp of back-half B&I growth, so this is a tone-and-FY27 item more than a Q3 revenue item.

text: ABM Aviation grew 19.5% in Q2 and its CEO warned on 2026-06-05 that 'rising fuel costs will likely create some near-term challenges for our airline clients'; since then the airline cost shock deepened rather than resolved - American Airlines cut FY26 guidance a second time in July (to a -$0.65 to +$0.65 adjusted EPS range from -$0.40 to +$1.10, with a Q3 loss guide, on ~$3.75/gal fuel), Southwest cut FY26 to $3.25-$4.25 from 'at least $4' after a ~$900m y/y Q2 fuel increase, and Alaska has had guidance suspended since April.
why_not_priced: Aviation is 13.5% of ABM revenue ($310.8m, $16.3m segment operating profit in Q2) and was the second-fastest-growing segment, and the market is extrapolating the Heathrow ramp. Airline distress is completely priced in airline equities - it is not priced in a name screened as defensive facility services, and none of the three published ABM estimates models an airline procurement squeeze on outsourced cabin, ground and passenger-assistance scope. If the market had priced it, ABM's 25-delta skew would be visibly bid for downside and the stock would be more than 4.68% off its high with realised vol above 15%. Sized small on purpose and honestly: TSA throughput set records through June and July 2026 so in-quarter volumes were fine, the direct Q3 EPS arithmetic of even a 5% Aviation revenue shortfall is roughly a penny, most ABM airline contracts pass through labour, and the industry capacity trim was already partly visible before ABM guided on 2026-06-05. The risk here is to forward commentary and FY27 framing, not to the Q3 number.

text: Note 8 of the Q2 FY26 10-Q states that ABM performed its review of the majority of its casualty insurance programmes during Q2 2026 and 'it was determined that there was no adjustment required for our total reserves related to prior years during the six months ended April 30, 2026' - so the item that produced a $(22.2)m pre-tax hit (~100bp of adjusted EBITDA margin, ~$0.26/sh) in Q4 FY25 is a Q2/Q4 event and is very unlikely to appear in the Q3 print, even though ABM's adjusted EPS definition now includes it while its guidance range is stated 'before any impact from prior-year self-insurance adjustments'.
why_not_priced: ABM changed its non-GAAP definition after SEC staff comment (disclosed 2025-12-17) so that reported adjusted EPS now INCLUDES prior-year self-insurance adjustments, while the $3.85-$4.15 guide explicitly excludes them. That mismatch is the mechanical reason FY25 landed at $3.44 against a $3.65-$3.80 range, and it is the most plausible single source of a headline 'miss' on this name. Three analysts on a $2.8bn company are not reading Note 8 of a June 10-Q to work out the actuarial cadence, and there is no aggregator field for 'timing of casualty reserve reviews'. If the market had priced the absence of this risk you would not see an indicative 8.13% implied move on a 93-contract chain with a 1.32 put/call OI ratio. This is a left-tail-removal finding, not a mean finding, which is why it is [sizing note removed].

Waterdrop's entire revenue growth story is one line: technical service income went RMB1.8m (Q4 2024) to RMB9.4m (Q1 2025) to RMB639.6m (Q4 2025) to RMB421.0m (Q1 2026) -- so it already fell 34.2% sequentially in Q1 2026 -- while brokerage income, the actual insurance business, was RMB648.6m / RMB670.8m / RMB724.8m over the same span, i.e. +11.7% YoY against the +64.8% headline, with sales and marketing rising from 22.9% to 43.6% of revenue and net profit falling to RMB98.4m from RMB108.2m.
why_not_priced: The decomposition requires subtracting the disclosed technical service line out of 'insurance-related income' -- a subtraction no aggregator performs, because every wire, Chinese and English, reprints the two headline numbers (+64.8% revenue, +74.1% insurance-related income) and stops. If the market had done the arithmetic, the last print on 2026-06-17 would not have paid +2.34% for a quarter in which net profit fell 9.1% YoY and the sole growth engine turned down 34% QoQ; there would be a published EPS consensus (there is none), and the only sell-side note on the tape would not be a UOB Kay Hian buy at US$2.20 dated 2025-03-14 (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/WDH/waterdrop-inc-receives-a-buy-rating-from-uob-kay-hian-with-price-lcl1sqnsy0x3.html), eighteen months stale and citing FY2024 net profit growth of 119.8%. The company has never disclosed the composition or counterparties of the line; its stated definition includes 'marketing services to insurance companies, insurance brokers, and agency companies', i.e. a gross-up of resold traffic, which is exactly why S&M rose 213.8% for 5.3% more operating profit.

Nothing connects it to WDH: there is no shared analyst, no sector note, and WDH's 20d run-up is +2.0%, i.e. the tape did not move on 2026-08-20. If the read-through were priced, WDH would have traded down that week rather than sitting pinned at $0.99-$1.00.

text: Waterdrop will report Q2 2026 with no CFO (vacant since Kangping Shi left in June 2022), no head of finance (Xiaoying Xu resigned as VP of finance and head of finance effective 2026-07-31), and a replacement audit-committee financial expert who took the seat only on 2026-07-01 after Heping Feng resigned from the audit, compensation and nominating committees -- two finance-governance exits inside 30 days, both immediately after the FY2025 20-F carrying the undisclosed RMB639.6m revenue line.
why_not_priced: The two events were reported separately and framed positively or neutrally by the only outlets that touched them: the director change was written up as 'Waterdrop Names New Independent Director and Audit Chair as Board Reshuffles' (TipRanks) and the finance exit as an AI-investment question by Simply Wall St (https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/insurance/nyse-wdh/waterdrop/news/what-does-waterdrops-wdh-finance-exit-reveal-about-its-ai-in). Nobody has put the two 6-Ks next to each other, or next to the fact that the top finance job has been unfilled for four years. If the cluster were priced, the 2026-07-24 session would carry a volume spike -- it does not; the stock closed $1.12 that day, mid-range, and drifted.

text: The US$50 million share repurchase authorisation expires on 2026-09-09 -- the day after this print -- with the great majority unused (cumulative buybacks moved only from US$118.1m to US$120.1m between the Q4 and Q1 releases, and the 20-F puts usage under the September 2025 programme at US$9.5m as of 2026-03-31), and Waterdrop has launched a new programme in September 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 and declared a US$0.03/ADS cash dividend alongside both its Q2 2025 and Q4 2025 results.
why_not_priced: The expiry date lives in one sentence of a twelve-month-old press release and appears in no calendar, no aggregator and no options market -- there is no options market on this name at all, so there is no mechanism by which a known forward event gets discounted here. A fresh authorisation of up to US$50m is roughly 11-14% of the US$366m market cap and about 190 sessions of the 254,685-ADS average volume, on a stock whose US$417.6m cash position exceeds its market cap. If this were priced, the run-in would not be +2.7% over five days off a 52-week low; a name with a near-certain buyback renewal and a ~6% annualised declared dividend yield would not be pinned at $0.99. The low end of my range is negative because the board has a live reason to skip the dividend this time: US$0.03 is 2.9% of a $1.02 spot and the ex-date would mechanically push the price under $1.00, so a dividend the holder base has come to expect could instead be cut or deferred.

text: WDH's NYSE Rule 802.01C 30-trading-day average closing price is $1.0263 as of 2026-09-04 (window 2026-07-27 to 2026-09-04), and the five sessions rolling out of that window closed $1.15/$1.15/$1.15/$1.14/$1.12, so the next five closes must average at least $0.984 to keep the average above $1.00 -- roughly 3.5% of cushion from the $1.02 spot, with the print the only scheduled catalyst inside that window.
why_not_priced: This is a computation, not a disclosure: it requires taking 30 daily closes and averaging them, and no company release, no aggregator field and no wire story states it. The eye-catching detail in the same series is that WDH closed at exactly $1.00 for thirteen consecutive sessions (2026-08-05 to 2026-08-21) and exactly $0.99 for the six after -- a pin, not a random walk, on a $260k/day notional. If the threshold were priced, the run-in would show either accelerating decline or a squeeze, not nineteen sessions of a flat line inside a one-cent band; and there would be an English-language story on it, of which there are none. Signed slightly negative because a $1.02 stock five sessions from a non-compliance notice has a fatter left tail on a bad print -- mandates that cannot hold non-compliant names sell -- while the offsetting 'management acts to support the price' channel is already carried in the buyback finding above.

text: The sweep's lead hypothesis -- an NFRA commission-cap or 'reporting and execution consistency' (bao xing he yi) enforcement action landing in the April-June 2026 quarter -- does not hold. The non-auto bao xing he yi regime took effect 2025-11-01 (http://www.news.cn/20251010/b8bbcefb0f3741889df474ed601f316b/c.html), and the regulator's unifying Q&A of January 2026 explicitly exempts short-term accident and health insurance, which is Waterdrop's fastest-growing FYP category (https://www.cnfin.com/hb-lb/detail/20260109/4362793_1.html). The one Q2-adjacent requirement, real-time settlement for high-frequency internet-scenario business, starts 2026-07-01, i.e. Q3 not Q2. No Q2 regulatory shock; if anything the exemption is why Waterdrop could push volume so hard.

The EU 21st-package carve-out that drove DLNG from $3.32 (16 July) to $3.85 (23 July) is a third-country-deliveries-only derogation expiring 25 July 2027, renewable one year at a time by Council vote and capped at the operator's 2025 volumes; the AIS work identifying the Dynagas vessels it protects names Clean Planet, Clean Vision, Clean Ocean and Clean Horizon - none of which are among the listed partnership's six ships - while DLNG's own Yamal-chartered Lena River last called at Huelva, Spain, an EU import terminal, departing 25 August 2026, i.e. exactly the EU-delivery employment the derogation does not cover.
why_not_priced: Dynagas holds no earnings call and has said nothing in writing since 29 May 2026, when its 6-K still stated that losing the Yamal charters 'would have a material adverse effect' and that it was studying 'the feasibility of lawfully removing the E.U. nexus'; the 8 September release is the first company text after the derogation. If the market had read the derogation's terms rather than the headline it would not have paid +9.17% and +4.34% on 22-23 July and then held most of it - and a $135m MLP with no analyst coverage, no EPS estimate and 41 contracts of total option open interest has no mechanism through which anyone reconciled the Official Journal text with which four hulls actually sit inside the listed entity. Coverage, if this were priced, would look like a note distinguishing the sponsor's Arc7 fleet from the MLP's 1A fleet; no such note exists.

text: Clean Energy, the vessel DLNG moved onto a Rio Grande LNG charter 'at higher daily rates' at the end of April 2026, has sat at anchor in Southeast Asia in ballast (draught 8.9 m, speed 0.1 knots) with no destination and no ETA since departing Singapore Anchorage on 5 August 2026 - 33 days idle - while Arctic Aurora, still trading normally (loaded at Melkoya, Norway on 7 September for Klaipeda), is contracted to begin a second seven-year Rio Grande charter between September and November 2026, which would put a third of the six-ship fleet on hire to a project company whose Brownsville trains are not yet producing.
why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates AIS for a 50k-ADV MLP. This does not touch Q2 revenue - Q2 ended 30 June and time-charter hire is paid whether the ship moves or not - so the channel is the presentation's fleet-employment page and any disclosure of sublet or restructured arrangements with Rio Grande LNG, LLC, plus the Arctic Aurora delivery window. Had the market focused on it, a name whose entire equity story is charter counterparty quality would carry commentary on a pre-operational charterer holding two of six hulls; there is none, and the July rally treated the charter book as de-risked rather than concentrated. I am deliberately sizing this small because the contractual cash flow is unaffected.

text: Six directors of Dynagas LNG Partners filed initial Section 16 ownership statements on 18 and 30 March 2026, every one of them carrying event date 18 March 2026 - George Prokopiou reporting 15,595,000 common units and 35,526 GP units indirectly through Dynagas Holding Ltd (50.4% beneficial interest), Alexios Rodopoulos 500 units direct, Dimitrios Anagnostopoulos 'no securities owned' - even though the partnership is exempt from Section 16 as a foreign private issuer under Rule 3a12-3(b), filed a 20-F for FY2025 on 8 April 2026 and has continued filing 6-Ks rather than 10-Qs through 13 August 2026; no Form 4 has followed in the five and a half months since.
why_not_priced: I am filing this at zero because I could not resolve it, not because it is unimportant: it is a genuine contradiction in the filing record that I can document and cannot explain. A board that becomes Section 16 reporting normally means the issuer has concluded it no longer qualifies as a foreign private issuer, which would force 10-Q/10-K/8-K, US-GAAP-only reporting and proxy statements - or it is the compliance footprint of a transaction. Neither has surfaced. If the market had noticed, a $135m MLP would show speculation about domestic-filer conversion or a going-private, and the 8 September event would not be scheduled as a 6-K with no conference call. I refuse to guess a sign, so it carries no directional weight; the band is width, not a view.

text: Charter expiry cliff - the door the sweep pointed at - is closed: Yenisei River to Yamal Trade 2033, Lena River 2034, Clean Energy to Rio Grande from April 2026, Arctic Aurora to Rio Grande for ~7 years from Sept-Nov 2026, Ob River and Amur River to SEFE to 2028. Nothing rolls off in 2026-27 that is not already contracted forward, and coverage is 100%/100%/65% for 2026/27/28 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000131786126000029/f052926dlng6k.htm).

Distribution catalyst - there is none. The Q2 common distribution of $0.050 was already declared on 13 August 2026 and the Series A preferred distribution of $0.5625 (44th consecutive) on 23 July 2026, so the 8 September release carries no capital-return news (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/13/3344926/0/en/dynagas-lng-partners-lp-announces-cash-distribution-for-the-quarter-ended-june-30-2026-of-0-050-per-common-unit.html).

Late-report signal - none. DLNG has always reported Q2 in early September; Q2 2025 was released before the open on 8 September 2025, so 8 September 2026 is exactly on cadence, not a delay (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/09/03/3144042/0/en/Dynagas-LNG-Partners-LP-Announces-Date-for-the-Release-of-the-Second-Quarter-and-Six-Month-2025-Results.html).

The Fayard drydock story - the six Arc7 hulls named as booked into Denmark's Fayard yard in summer 2026 before the January 2027 EU maritime-services ban are Rudolf Samoylovich, Georgiy Brusilov, Boris Davydov, Vladimir Vize, Nikolay Zubov and Nikolay Yevgenov. None is a DLNG vessel, so the off-hire angle does not reach the MLP (https://www.urgewald.org/en/media/danish-shipyard-receives-first-six-russia-linked-arctic-lng-tankers-eu-maritime, 2026-07-02).

Sponsor take-private or unit accumulation - no SC 13D and no SC 13D/A has been filed since 2017 and there has been no Form 4 ever. The only 2026 ownership filing is a passive SCHEDULE 13G by an individual, Thomas W. Herfort, for 1,901,981 units (5.17%), event date 4 August 2026, filed 11 August 2026 - real flow at ~38x average daily volume, but it is on EDGAR and was written up by aggregators, so I treat it as thinly priced rather than unpriced and give it no weight (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000119983526000285/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml).

Refinancing - the four sale-and-leaseback facilities with China Development Bank Financial Leasing (Clean Energy $38.6m, Ob River $51.2m, Amur River $52.7m ~3 years each, Arctic Aurora $125.2m ~9 years, $266.2m total) amortise rather than balloon, $11.0m repaid in Q1 2026, so there is no maturity wall for a refinancing announcement to clear.

The company's own website (dynagaspartners.com, including the /upload_press/ PDF path and the Presentations page) returned HTTP 503 on every attempt on 2026-09-07, and the Wayback API has no snapshot of the presentations page, so I could not front-run the slide deck or diff the fleet table on the company's own pages.

Yamal-side operational distress that would reach DLNG's P&L - Bellona's AIS-derived monthly Arctic report for May 2026 counts 25 Sabetta cargoes to Belgium, France, the Netherlands and Spain and names no Dynagas vessel; and because both Yamal ships are on time charter to 2033/2034, the fact that Yenisei River was drifting at 1.9 knots off southwest Ireland and Lena River was steaming 'FOR ORDERS' on 6-7 September 2026 costs the partnership no hire (https://etc.bellona.org/2026/07/09/monthly-highlights-from-the-russian-arctic-may-2026/, https://www.vesselfinder.com/vessels/details/9629598).

A quantifiable Q2 revenue surprise - the arithmetic is already public and roughly offsetting: Q1 2026 carried off-hire from unscheduled repairs on two vessels (95.1% utilisation vs 98.8% in Q4 2025) which should not repeat, against roughly three weeks of Clean Energy redelivery gap in April 2026 inside Q2. Q1 revenue was $39.9m and adjusted EBITDA $24.3m; I have no basis to call Q2 materially away from that.

UNFI's own narrowed FY26 guide implies Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $156-176mm, but the company itself quantified the prior-year Q4 as depressed by $40-50mm of cyber-incident adjusted EBITDA, so on a cyber-clean basis Q4 FY26 EBITDA is roughly flat to +13% (mid ~+3%) against reported growth of +34% to +52%, and against +23.4% in Q2 and +16.6% in Q3 — the underlying run-rate that has to support a ~$745-760mm FY27 guide on the way to the $800mm FY28 Investor Day target has decelerated to near zero.
why_not_priced: The arithmetic requires stitching three documents together: 39-week actuals (26-week adj EBITDA $346mm from the 2026-03-10 8-K plus $183mm Q3 from the 2026-06-09 8-K = $529mm), the narrowed FY26 guide of $685-705mm, and the July 2025 8-K's $40-50mm cyber EBITDA quantification. If the market had done it, the published Q4 consensus would not be sitting exactly on the guide midpoint (rev $7.705bn vs guide-implied $7.590-7.790bn; EPS $0.612 vs guide-implied $0.45-0.65, i.e. the 81st percentile of the company's own range) — consensus is modelling the reported optic, not the clean run-rate, and there is no visible FY27 whisper on a name the aggregators show with 2 estimates.

text: SNAP enrollment fell from 42.2 million in May 2025 to 36.6 million in May 2026 (-13%, faster than CBO projected, with Arizona -55%, Florida -22%), and this data was published on 2026-08-21 — after UNFI last guided on 2026-06-09; UNFI's Conventional ($3.136bn) plus Retail ($515mm) segments were ~47% of Q3 FY26 net sales and are precisely the SNAP-exposed channels.
why_not_priced: UNFI is modelled as a natural/organic growth story, not a SNAP name — its Q3 narrative and the sell-side framing are Natural segment growth and network optimisation, and management has never quantified SNAP exposure on a call. If this were priced into UNFI specifically you would see Conventional-segment estimates cut and the FY27 sales bridge debated; instead UNFI reiterated its FY26 midpoints on 2026-06-09 and the coverage that followed argued about the revenue miss, not the channel. The SNAP theme is priced into Kroger/Dollar General; it is not priced into the wholesaler two steps upstream.

text: Both listed natural-channel retailers reported negative traffic inside UNFI's Q4 window (2026-05-03 to 2026-08-01): Natural Grocers' quarter ended 2026-06-30 showed daily-average comps +1.2% built entirely on a +3.1% basket with transaction count -1.8% and gross margin down 60bp, and Sprouts' June quarter showed comps -1% with management citing weaker June trends — while UNFI's Natural segment (+4.4% in Q3) is the only growing part of the company and the pillar of the FY27 return-to-growth guide.
why_not_priced: Nobody carries UNFI and NGVC in the same model — NGVC is a $335mm-a-quarter retailer and UNFI is a $31bn wholesaler, and the read-through runs the wrong way for a screener. If the market had made this link, the negative-unit-volume debate would be in the UNFI previews (which instead lead on the easy cyber comp and the +$0.62-vs-$(0.11) EPS optic) and UNFI's Natural-segment growth estimate would have been cut after 2026-08-06. NGVC itself fell 14% on the print, so the channel datapoint moved a price — just not this one.

text: Amazon's physical-stores net sales — the reported line for Whole Foods, UNFI's largest customer at roughly a quarter of net sales — were $5,794mm in the June-2026 quarter versus $5,595mm a year earlier, +4% and +4% excluding FX, essentially unchanged from the +4.6% March-quarter pace, covering two-thirds of UNFI's Q4.
why_not_priced: Customer concentration is the standing bear case on UNFI and the reason the put skew sits at +6.97 points, but the one hard, contemporaneous, third-party measurement of that customer's volume during the quarter being reported sits in an Amazon 8-K exhibit that no UNFI preview cites. If it were priced, the previews would say Whole Foods sell-through was steady through July rather than treating the Whole Foods exposure as an unmeasured risk; instead the risk is discussed only through the 2032 contract term. It also removes one of the two live explanations for a Q4 revenue miss, leaving only the deliberate Allentown/Sturtevant optimisation.

text: UNFI pulled its Q4/full-year report forward roughly three weeks against a stable four-year pattern — 2026-09-08 versus 2025-09-30, 2024-10-01 and late September in the two prior years — and announced the new date on 2026-08-10, the exact day the incoming CFO started, five and a half weeks after a 1 August fiscal year end.
why_not_priced: Calendar aggregators carry the date, not the change in the date — the row reads 2026-09-08 with no memory that this company has reported Q4 in the last week of September or the first day of October every year since FY2022, so the timing shift leaves no trace in coverage or in the option chain. A company finalising a full-year audit and a fresh long-range plan five and a half weeks after year end, with a CFO four weeks into the job, is not behaving like one that needs time. I am scoring this small because I could not rule out the benign explanation: Barclays' Global Consumer Staples Conference runs 2026-09-09, the day after, and staples issuers routinely report just ahead of it — I could not confirm UNFI on that agenda either way.

text: The initial FY27 guide — the single largest swing factor in this print — will be delivered by a CFO who started on 2026-08-10, four weeks before, as part of four senior changes in seven weeks around the fiscal year end: Matteo Tarditi moved off CFO to President/COO, Alfredo Luchini arrived as CFO from Carrier, supply-chain head Mark Bushway was announced as departing 2027-01-01, and Chief Corporate Affairs Officer Matthew Echols ceased in the role on 2026-08-24.
why_not_priced: The personnel facts are in an 8-K, but the consequence for this specific print is not in any preview: UNFI's two 20%-class up-moves (2024-12-10 +20.02%, 2025-09-30 +18.45%) were both guide-setting prints delivered by Tarditi, who set FY26 deliberately low ($1.50-2.30 adjusted EPS) and raised the midpoint to $2.50 over three quarters. A first-print CFO inheriting a public $800mm FY28 target he did not set has an asymmetric incentive to anchor FY27 at the bottom of that path. If the market had focused on this, the 12.5% implied would be skewed toward a guidance-reset outcome rather than symmetric around a spot 21% off the high, and previews would be discussing who owns the FY27 number.

Short-squeeze fuel — short interest is 2.65mm shares / 4.48% of float at 2026-08-14 versus 3.8-3.95mm shares before the 2024-12-10 +20.02% print (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/UNFI/short-interest/), so the crowding that amplified the historical up-tails is materially smaller

Food-at-home inflation inflecting — BLS food-at-home CPI was +2.7% y/y in July 2026 and flat month-on-month, essentially the same pricing backdrop UNFI described in Q3, so no inflation surprise to the wholesale sales dollar
A large customer loss or win beyond the already-disclosed Key Food exit and the single-customer project that management said cycles by Q3 FY2027

Whether UNFI is on the Barclays Global Consumer Staples 2026-09-09 agenda, which would fully explain the report-date pull-forward — could not confirm either way from the conference schedule or UNFI IR

UNFI's fuel hedge book is a $5m Level-2 current asset as of 2026-05-02 (up from $1m at 2026-01-31) - trivially small against a $1.87/gal year-over-year diesel move - and being entirely current it expires inside FY27, exactly the year whose guide is set on 8 September, with US on-highway diesel at $5.599/gal on 2026-08-31 (+$1.865 YoY) after having fallen to $4.578 on 2026-07-06.
why_not_priced: On the 9 June call management named 'fuel hedging' first of three mitigation levers when pressed on fuel by R5 Capital, and that framing is what the market is working from; the 10-Q fair-value table shows the hedge is a $5m current asset, i.e. immaterial and expiring, and the DERIVATIVES note itself lists only interest-rate swaps so a reader of the note alone would never see the fuel book at all. If the market had read this, a preview would describe the hedge as de minimis rather than as a mitigant, and the two-estimate FY27 consensus would carry an explicit fuel line. The separate and larger point the price cannot yet hold is the path: diesel fell to $4.578 in early July, making the fuel scare look resolved, then re-spiked to a record, so the fuel curve against which the FY27 guide must be set is materially worse than the one visible when management last spoke. I am discounting heavily because the -4.08% five-day run-in overlaps the week diesel set its record, which is evidence the market is pricing some of this.

text: Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage, which buys 69% of its product from UNFI, reported its quarter ended 2026-06-30 - sitting entirely inside UNFI's Q4 - with net sales up only 1.8%, daily average transaction COUNT down 1.8%, gross margin down 60bp on unfavourable mix and higher freight, and cut the top end of both its FY26 EPS guide ($2.15 to $2.11) and its comp guide (2.5% to 2.0%), all against a prior-year base that its own release says was distorted by the cybersecurity incident at its primary distributor.
why_not_priced: NGVC's release never names UNFI, and nothing bridges a small natural-foods retailer's 8-K to a $2.7bn wholesaler's Q4 - UNFI carries two published estimates, so there is no mechanism by which such a read-through gets marked. If it were priced you would see UNFI's natural-segment growth expectation publicly stepped down from the +4.4% posted in Q3, and there is no revision note doing that. The specific unpriced content is the direction of units: NGVC grew dollars 1.8% while shrinking traffic 1.8% against a comp depressed by UNFI's own June-2025 outage, which implies natural-channel case volume in UNFI's Q4 was weaker than the Q3 exit rate rather than stronger.

text: Five senior officer changes between 2026-07-09 and 2026-08-24 - CFO Matteo Tarditi moved to President/COO, Louis Martin to Chief Commercial Officer, external hire Alfredo Luchini (ex-Carrier) became CFO on 2026-08-10, Chief Supply Chain Officer Mark Bushway exits 2027-01-01, and Chief Corporate Affairs Officer Matthew Echols ceased to serve on 2026-08-24 - so a CFO four weeks into the seat delivers UNFI's first multi-year guide, and the Echols departure was disclosed only in an exit Form 4 with no 8-K and no press release.
why_not_priced: The Echols exit exists only as a Form 4 with no transactions and a single footnote, filed 2026-08-27 - there is no press release and no 8-K item 5.02 for it, so no news aggregator, no Zacks note and no wire preview carries it, and the count of C-suite changes is therefore understated everywhere the market looks. On the guide itself: with two published FY27 estimates there is no consensus number visible against which a conservative first guide could already be marked, so 'new CFO resets the base' cannot be in the price the way it would be on a twenty-analyst name, where you would see a pre-print estimate cut cluster. What holds this finding down, and why the band crosses zero, is that the print was pulled forward roughly three weeks from the late-September/early-October date UNFI used in each of the prior three years (last year's Q4 release was 2025-09-30), landing 38 days after fiscal year end - reporting early with a month-old CFO argues for a clean, confident close rather than a reset.

text: Whole Foods / Amazon primary distribution agreement - runs to May 2032 after the May 2024 eight-year extension, no near-term renewal risk and nothing new since (https://www.unfi.com/news-and-resources/articles/news/unfi-contract-renewal-whole-foods-market.html)

Retail-segment divestiture: no assets-held-for-sale line on the 2026-05-02 balance sheet (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1020859/000102085926000015/R2.htm), and the only retail action since is three Cub stores sold to franchisee Jerry's Enterprises on 2026-08-17, terms undisclosed and immaterial (https://www.grocerydive.com/news/unfi-selling-cub-foods-stores-jerrys-minneapolis-grocery-supermarkets/828011/)
Activist or strategic-review stake - the only ownership filing since June is a routine Vanguard Capital Management Schedule 13G filed 2026-07-31

New WARN filings / unannounced DC closures after the Q3 print - the only 2026 action is Sturtevant WI (443 jobs, WARN filed 2026-03-16, separations completed by mid-August), announced before the Q3 print and therefore priced

Labour disruption into the print - the one 2026 dispute (Teamsters Local 769, Pompano Beach, ~200 workers) was settled with a five-year contract ratified 2026-04-17; teamster.org shows no UNFI item in July, August or September 2026
Cyber-incident insurance recovery as a hidden FY26 EBITDA item - the $26m of direct FY25 costs were already added back in the FY25 reconciliation, so any recovery is immaterial against a $695m base

Term-loan repricing as a finding - Amendment No. 5 of 2026-06-18 cut the margin on ~$371m from SOFR+4.75% to SOFR+4.00%, roughly $2.8m a year, too small to matter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001020859/000102085926000017/unfi-20260618.htm)
Food-at-home CPI as a revenue tailwind - +2.7% YoY in July 2026 and flat month-on-month, i.e. consistent with the 'low single-digit inflation' UNFI already guides to, no surprise either way

Quantifying UNFI's annual diesel gallons - Item 7A of the FY2025 10-K would not render through any fetch path I tried, so the fuel exposure in finding 1 is sized off the hedge asset's fair value rather than off consumption

A non-obvious upside catalyst - no source anywhere points to a first buyback authorisation or a raise to the December 2025 Investor Day targets (~$33bn sales, ~$800m adjusted EBITDA, ~$300m FCF for FY28), and that release explicitly directs cash to network, capabilities and balance sheet instead

Canaan's self-mining run-rate halved entering Q3 while it reported installed hashrate as flat: monthly BTC produced went 90 (April) / 90 (May) / 64 (June) / 46 (July) = 3.00 / 2.90 / 2.13 / 1.48 BTC per day, a 51% per-day decline, driven by Ethiopia (4.96 EH/s, a third of the 14.9 EH/s installed fleet) falling from 2.33 EH/s operating at 30 April to 0.36 EH/s at 30 June and then being described as 'paused' at 31 July -- yet the July release counted the entire paused 4.96 EH/s inside its headline 'operating computing power' of 14.24 EH/s, one month after the same table had shown Ethiopia at 0.36 EH/s operating.
why_not_priced: Reported Q2 mining volume (90+90+64 = 244 BTC vs 257 in Q1) will look almost flat, so the deterioration is invisible in the quarter being reported and only shows up in the Q3-to-date commentary and any Q3 guide. If the market had underwritten it, the stock would not have risen 68% in the 20 sessions that straddle the 17 August release of the 46-BTC month; the two named drivers of that rally were the 20 August Trump/CLARITY Act crypto bid and the 25-27 August Bitcoin Asia conference, i.e. sector beta and a trade show. Coverage is two EPS estimates and a 'Strong Buy' consensus with a $1.72 target on a $0.36 stock, so nobody is modelling site-level uptime. The August production 6-K, on the company's own mid-month cadence (April update 14 May, May update 11 June, June update 14 July, July update 17 August), falls after the 8 September print, so the print is the first place an August number or an Ethiopia explanation can surface.

text: Canaan converted its automatic shelf into a $270m standard Form F-3 on 15 April 2026 specifically because it 'expects that it will cease to be a well-known seasoned issuer' on filing its FY2025 20-F, then filed Post-Effective Amendment No. 5 on 15 June 2026 as an 'exhibits-only filing to file an updated auditor consent' -- i.e. it is actively keeping a shelf equal to roughly its entire market value usable -- against cash that fell from US$80.8m at 31 December 2025 to US$43.5m at 31 March 2026, a Q1 gross LOSS of US$22.9m, US$21.1m short-term debt, and zero 424B5 takedowns anywhere in 2026 after three in 2025 (March, October, November).
why_not_priced: An exhibits-only post-effective amendment to refresh an auditor consent generates no headline, no wire story and no aggregator row -- it is pure plumbing whose only purpose is to keep the shelf sellable, and it is not in the +68% run-up. If the market were pricing takedown risk you would see it in the skew, and there is no two-sided ATM option chain here at all. The specific asymmetry is timing: after ten months without using the shelf while burning ~US$37m of cash in a single quarter, the first 68% rally in a year is the first usable equity window, and a pre-open results release with an 8:00 a.m. call is where issuers of this type disclose one.

text: There is a mid-June 2026 open-market insider buy cluster that is essentially invisible for this name because Canaan is a 20-F/6-K filer whose officers nonetheless file Section 16 forms: CFO Cheng Jin bought 65,000 ADSs at US$0.35 on 15 June, and CEO Nangeng Zhang bought 250,000 ADSs at US$0.34 on 17 June and 250,000 at US$0.33 on 18 June, and no insider has filed any transaction since 22 June -- no sales at all into the 68% rally.
why_not_priced: Insider-transaction screens and the sell-side notes on this name are built around the FPI assumption that a 20-F filer has no Section 16 reporting at all, so these Form 4s are not in any Canaan coverage I could find; had they been picked up, a CEO buying half a million ADSs three days before the low would have generated at least one wire story, and it generated none. It is also stale by twelve weeks and the purchase prices (US$0.33-0.35) sit essentially at today's US$0.36, which is exactly why I size it under one point rather than treating it as a signal about the print.

text: Canaan is inside its second and final Nasdaq minimum-bid-price compliance period, expiring 11 January 2027, with the ADSs at US$0.36 -- needing roughly +178% and then ten consecutive closes at or above US$1.00 -- and the company has committed to nothing more than that it 'will evaluate all available options during the second compliance period to rectify the deficiency'; I found no depositary notice of any Canaan reverse split or ADS-ratio change, and an ADS-ratio change (currently 1 ADS = 15 Class A shares) needs no shareholder vote and can be effected in weeks.
why_not_priced: The deficiency itself IS in the wire and is priced; what is not priced is that with about four months and one earnings call left, the 8 September pre-open release is the natural and cheapest venue to announce a ratio change, and the company has so far declined to name the remedy. If the market had positioned for it there would be visible put demand -- instead the chain has no two-sided ATM legs at all and put/call open interest is 0.03, i.e. essentially no downside protection outstanding. I sized this at only one point because it is a mechanical, disclosed clock rather than new information.

text: Any 424B5 or ATM prospectus supplement filed by Canaan in 2026 (full EDGAR submissions list checked; last was 2025-11-04), so no evidence of actual 2026 dilution, only capacity and motive
Any depositary notice of a Canaan reverse split or ADS-ratio change (the two Citi notices search returned were NIP Group Inc. and Nobia AB, not Canaan)
An August 2026 bitcoin-production 6-K -- none filed as of 2026-09-07; on the company's mid-month cadence it falls after the print

Any 2026-dated report that Ethiopian Electric Power has formally terminated or repriced Canaan's specific power contract; the EEP phase-out statements I could source are from August 2025 and the October 2025 tariff change, and I am not treating them as new
Any 10-Q, 10-K or item 2.02 8-K for Canaan -- it still files 20-F/6-K only, so there is no quarterly footnote text to diff against the prior quarter
Any disclosed completed buyback volume or dollar amount; the 4 August release and the 17 August update both stop at authorisation
Any insider Form 4 filed after 2026-06-22, in either direction, including through the 68% August rally
Any EGM/proxy notice, going-private proposal or 13D-style activist filing (only passive 13G/13G-A filings on 2026-06-05, 08-11 and 08-13)
Customer-side surfaces that exist for consumer names but not for a rig vendor: no app-store reviews, no support forum with a live complaint thread, no status page
Any government contract award, port or shipping datapoint tying to A15/A16 rig shipment volumes

Cipher Mining's 53,762,660 CAN ADSs (806,439,900 Class A shares, ~9.2% of the 585.8m reported float), issued to it at US$0.7394/ADS on 2026-02-23 as payment for the ABC Projects JV stake, came out of lock-up on 2026-08-23 -- Cipher's own 10-Q states the date and carries the position inside 'Prepaid expenses and other current assets', and the shares were never registered for resale, so Cipher can sell under Rule 144 as a non-affiliate with no volume cap and no Form 144 trail.
why_not_priced: The block is invisible to every screen that quotes this name: stockanalysis.com's float of 585.80m excludes it, Canaan's own EDGAR filer index shows no Schedule 13G or 13D from Cipher (CIK 1819989) among the 13Gs on file, Canaan filed no resale registration for it (the 2026-05-22 POS AM to F-3 333-285125 is a $270m primary shelf and names no selling shareholder), and Cipher as a non-affiliate owes no Form 144. If the market had focused on it, CAN would not have risen 68% in 20 days straight through the expiry date with a 9%-of-float unregistered block coming loose, and the 25-delta skew would exist at all rather than the chain being one-sided and untradeable. Instead the tape only began to show it three sessions before the print: CAN closed 2026-09-04 down 8.47% on a day bitcoin rose 2.26% to $79,697. Cipher has already written the stake down from $39.75m (a $16.5m fair-value loss booked in Q1 alone), is funding an AI/HPC datacentre conversion at the same Black Pearl site whose rigs it sold, and has classified the holding as a current asset -- three reasons it monetises into the highest-volume session this stock will see, which is the print.

text: The 2026-08-04 'repurchase shares using digital asset treasury' release that lit the +68% run adds no new authorisation and no dollar figure -- it points back to a US$30m board authorisation dated 2025-12-12 that expires 2026-12-12 and that Canaan's own Q1 release says had bought only ~2.8m ADSs for ~US$2.0m (6.7%), after the prior US$30m programme executed just US$4.9m (16%); the Sept 8 release is the first document that must state repurchases through 30 June.
why_not_priced: The wire treated it as a new programme -- headlines read 'Canaan authorizes crypto sales to fund $30 million share repurchase program' -- and the stock rose 12.43% that session and has not given the gain back. If the market had checked utilisation it would have priced an option worth ~$28m of residual capacity on a company that has used 16% and then 6.7% of two consecutive identical authorisations while its Class A count rose 806m shares, i.e. net issuer not net repurchaser over the exact life of the 'buyback'. If this were priced, the >110% NDR line would be treated as de-risked rather than as the swing factor, and the 25-delta skew would not be paying for downside.

So the run-in is group beta, not the market pre-positioning for a bad Sunbelt quarter. text: Culp issued its Q1 FY27 guidance on 2026-07-01 for a quarter that ended 2026-08-02 - i.e. with roughly 9 of 13 weeks already elapsed and the $7.0m tariff refund cash already in hand - so 'breakeven to positive adjusted EBITDA without the benefit of IEEPA tariff refunds' and 'net debt of approximately $5.0 million by first quarter-end' are near-observed facts, not forecasts.
why_not_priced: The baseline's expected move is a 6.02% median drawn from seven prints of which six went down - all of them delivered mid-restructuring with no forward guidance and genuinely uncertain outcomes. This print is the opposite: the guide was set two-thirds of the way through the quarter with the one-time cash already received. If the market had processed that the outcome distribution is narrow, the run-up would not be a directionless -0.58% over 20 days and the 5-day drift would not be a 17,000-share-a-day random walk; a stock about to resolve a genuinely uncertain 6% event trades differently into it. The residual is that Culp's downside tail here is much thinner than its own reaction history implies.

text: Culp presents adjusted EBITDA and 'non-GAAP operating loss' but no adjusted-EPS line at all, so the $7.0m IEEPA refund - 16% of the $43m market cap - flows into the single headline GAAP diluted EPS figure that wires will compare directly against the $0.44 estimate, with no adjusted/GAAP mismatch to manufacture a fake miss.
why_not_priced: The default failure mode when a microcap books a one-time gain of this size is that the company headlines an ex-item loss and the tape prints a catastrophic-looking miss against a GAAP-basis estimate. That risk is real enough that if the market had checked it the estimate dispersion would show it - instead there is a single point estimate at $0.44 and no visible hedging. I checked the reconciliation captions in the company's own last release and the mismatch does not exist. This is a removed negative tail rather than new upside, which is why it is sized small.

text: AEO will report GAAP EPS several times the $0.21 consensus purely mechanically — it told CNBC on 2026-06-03 it had already received $108m of IEEPA refunds, its 10-Q says the amount plus any further refunds will be recorded as a reduction of cost of sales for the 13 weeks ending 2026-08-01, and guidance explicitly excludes it — but the 2Q26 retail season's own base rate is that the market strips these out: Kohl's fell about 6% on a $150m refund and a raised full-year outlook, Target's stock fell on a beat containing $1.65/share of refund, and the only large positive reaction (ANF +36%) came with a 23% underlying beat ex-refund.
why_not_priced: This is a correction to a mispricing of the *reaction function*, not of the fact. AEO's own tape shows the read-across is unresolved: the stock rose 5.14% on 2026-08-26 (ANF's refund-driven print) and gave back 5.12% on 2026-08-27, a clean round trip to zero, and the 20-day run-up is -0.78%. That pattern is what an unsettled question looks like, not a priced one. If the market had settled it in the bullish direction the run-up would be positive and the skew would be call-bid; if it had settled it bearishly there would be no 5% up-day. The consequence is that the near-certain 3x headline beat is not the catalyst a naive reading of the six-estimate consensus implies, and the resulting full-year operating-income raise from ~$390-410m to ~$500m+ will be discounted as a non-recurring item that has to be lapped in 2027.

If the market had connected them, the coverage would frame tonight as a rebasing event rather than a beat-or-miss on $0.21, and a stock 38.9% off its high with a plan needing a 4.3x second-half ramp would carry more than a 6.6-point 25-delta skew on 188% ATM implied vol, which is proportionally flat for an event of this kind. Note the offset that is genuinely priced: the company reaffirmed both Q2 and full-year guidance in this same release on 2026-07-01, which caps how bad the Q2 underlying can plausibly be.

text: Fiscal Q2 2027 is a structurally mismatched quarter: it covers 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-31, during which the Fed did not move (held 3.50-3.75% on 2026-07-29, unchanged since December 2025) so no rate benefit accrued, while Wealthfront Home Lending only launched in California and Texas on 2026-08-11 — after quarter end — meaning the full pre-launch mortgage build cost sits in Q2 with essentially zero mortgage revenue, on top of Q1 GAAP expenses already up 46% year-over-year to $75.9m against 7% revenue growth.
why_not_priced: Coverage of the 2026-08-11 launch was uniformly framed as a growth event ('rates ~0.50% below the national average', expansion to FL/IL/OR/WA), not as a calendar problem for the quarter reporting three weeks later. A market that had done the date arithmetic would not have marked the stock up 8.97% in the five sessions into a print whose expense line carries a launch it cannot yet monetise; the run-up looks like a growth read, not a cost read. Wealthfront's 10-K states home lending revenue was immaterial in FY2026, so there is no offsetting revenue base.

text: Schwab disclosed on 2026-08-14 that transactional sweep cash fell $8.9bn in July 2026 to $476.8bn — 1.8% of the balance in one month — 'reflecting client net purchasing activity as well as typical seasonality related to advisory fee payments', and the S&P 500 then rose 2.7% in August to record highs; at Wealthfront a dollar migrating from cash to investing loses roughly 60% of its revenue (cash fee rate ~54bp vs investment advisory running ~21bp annualised on $26.2m of quarterly revenue against ~$50bn of advisory assets), so the same client behaviour that will produce a record platform-assets headline tonight is revenue-dilutive.
why_not_priced: Wealthfront publishes monthly metrics only for months one and two of each fiscal quarter — the last public flow datapoint is June, released 2026-07-07 (Cash Management Net Deposits -$235m). July and August flows are both released for the first time tonight. No WLTH-specific wire item connects Schwab's July sweep decline to Wealthfront's undisclosed July cash flow; if that link were priced you would see WLTH coverage referencing it and the stock would not be flat over 20 days while its cash-heavy revenue mix was being drained. Sized small and with a wide band because the read-across is genuinely ambiguous: June's -$235m is partly the 15 June estimated-tax date, and the S&P fell in both June and July, which normally favours cash.

text: The rate regime that defines this company's entire bear case has flipped: the FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% on 2026-07-29 with three regional presidents dissenting in favour of a 25bp HIKE, and futures price roughly 60% odds of a hike at the 2026-09-16 meeting one week after this print — while Wealthfront has held its base Cash Account APY at 3.30% since 2026-01-30 and its own 10-K states that 'in weaker macroeconomic environments with higher interest rates, our cash management products become more popular.'
why_not_priced: Every plaintiff-firm investigation opened on this name (BFA 2026-03-16, Pomerantz 2026-07-07, Robbins and Johnson Fistel 2026-08-20) alleges misstatements about 'interest rate sensitivity' and asset flows — the whole public narrative is that falling rates break the model. A price that had absorbed a live hike would not sit 31% below the $14 December 2025 IPO price and 30.8% below its 52-week high with the S&P at record highs. Management is near-certain to be asked to quantify hike sensitivity on a call held eight days before the FOMC, and has an unusually good answer for the first time since listing. I have discounted this from a larger number because the +8.97% five-day run-up, into the week of a strong August payroll print, is plausibly this trade already starting.

text: Tonight is a double-disclosure event, not a normal print: because Wealthfront publishes monthly metrics only for the first two months of each fiscal quarter, the 2026-08-19 scheduling release states that metrics 'through August 2026' will be posted with the results — meaning July (fiscal Q2's third month) and August (fiscal Q3's first month) flows both become public for the first time tonight, alongside the P&L.
why_not_priced: This is a variance finding, not a directional one, and I have given it zero expected impact deliberately. It matters because the baseline's option chain is unusable (609 total open interest, ATM bid-ask 127% of mid) so there is no priced statement of magnitude at all, and the only anchor is a three-event history of -16.84%, -6.19% and -14.35%. Two months of unseen flow data plus a quarter of P&L is exactly why this name's prints move double digits, and it argues the realised move will be at the wide end regardless of sign.

why_not_priced: There is one published estimate on the name (EPS -$0.02), no option chain at all, and the stock sits 1.2% off its 52-week low having drifted -10.2% over 20 days - a tape consistent with zero expectation of an EBITDA-positive quarter. Turnover of ~$10k/day means nothing here is arbitraged, which is why a mechanically derivable upstream read survives to the print.

why_not_priced: The wire frame on DSGX is that the February 2026 Supreme Court strike-down of IEEPA tariffs removes trade complexity and therefore demand -- that is the frame that took the stock 30% off its high and left puts bid. With only two published estimates there is no model that carries a PSC-volume line, and Descartes' guidance construct (a $169.0m contracted 'baseline' plus whatever transactional volume arrives) means this shows up exactly in the beat-over-baseline, which is the number the stock trades on.

text: Descartes deployed roughly $250m of cash on four weeks of M&A around quarter-end -- Drivin $30m on 2026-07-06 (in-quarter), Tai $100m on 2026-08-24 and Extensiv $120m on 2026-09-01 (both post-quarter, eight days apart) -- and Extensiv is a distressed-timeline asset: its $80m Runway Growth senior secured term loan matured 2026-06-30, 63 days before the sale, and the price is roughly 1.2-2.4x revenue against Descartes' own 46% adjusted-EBITDA-margin base.
why_not_priced: The announcements are public and the tape sold both of them (-1.21% on 24 Aug, -2.41% on 1 Sep in the sealed baseline), so the fact of the deals is priced. What is not priced is the size: neither press release discloses revenue, EBITDA or accretion, so nothing in consensus -- two estimates -- carries a number. why_not_priced: A $1m-salary EVP appointment in a routine item-5.02 8-K nine days before a print draws no wire coverage and no analyst note — I found no sell-side commentary linking it to the quarter. The mechanism the market is missing is timing, not the person: Foran's documented Walmart playbook is price investment funded by cost-out with near-term margin sacrifice, he has already said publicly he will cut prices broadly and double new-store openings to 70-80 next year, and a CEO does not import a Chief Store Operations Officer to keep executing an inherited plan. Guidance resets are overwhelmingly delivered once the new team is seated. If the market had focused on this, the print would carry a visible 'reset risk' premium in put skew rather than the -2.76 call-bid skew actually quoted.

text: The two peer prints that actually overlap Kroger's Q2 window (2026-05-24 to 2026-08-15) show the traffic going to mass and club, not to conventional supermarkets: Walmart U.S. comped +2.6% for the quarter ended 2026-07-31 led by transactions and RAISED FY27 guidance, and Costco's U.S. comp ex-gasoline and FX was +5.6% for the four weeks ended 2026-08-30 — against Kroger's own guide of identical sales 'roughly in line with the first quarter' at 1.0%.
why_not_priced: The read-across note the street actually wrote was on 2026-07-23, off Albertsons' guidance cut, and Albertsons' quarter ended 2026-06-20 — it covers only the first four weeks of Kroger's Q2 and says nothing about July or August. Walmart's May-July quarter and Costco's August month are the only public reads on the back two-thirds of Kroger's quarter, and nobody re-ran the read-across on them because Walmart's print was framed as a Walmart story (tariff refunds, e-commerce, guidance raise). The distinction matters directionally: a soft-industry quarter is forgivable and a share-loss quarter is not, and share loss is what forces a price-investment reset. Had this been priced, Kroger would not be flat (+1.5%) over 20 days while Walmart raised guidance in the middle of that window.

text: Grocery dollar inflation is running materially hotter in Kroger's Q2 window than in the Q1 window that management extrapolated from: food-at-home CPI was +1.9% y/y in March 2026 but +2.7% y/y in each of May, June and July 2026, so Kroger's 'roughly in line with the first quarter' 1.0% identical-sales guide, set on 2026-06-18, embeds roughly 50-60bp less price than the quarter is actually carrying.
why_not_priced: This is the one leg that cuts upward and it is the reason the answer is -2.3 and not -4. It is public and free, but the previews all quote the EPS consensus rather than the comp, and Kroger's identical-sales line is the number this stock trades on. Management guided the comp on 2026-06-18 with only March and April CPI in hand; June and July food-at-home prints (both +2.7%) landed after. Two of the eight prints in the reaction history were up 5%+ on a comp beat, so a 150-160bp comp against a 100bp guide is a real upside path that the -2.76 call-bid skew is arguably already leaning toward — which is exactly why I am sizing it as a partial offset rather than the headline.

Oracle has sold ZERO shares under its $20bn at-the-market common equity program: the FY2026 10-K tags 'Common stock shares sold' under the ATM Offering member as 0, and the FY2026 cash flow statement shows only $1,449m of common stock proceeds (ESPP/option exercises) against $4,954m of mandatory convertible preferred and $46,093m of notes/term loans - yet on 2026-06-23, one day after filing the 10-K, Oracle filed a 424B5 adding roughly ten further sales agents to that same $20bn program, and shares outstanding are still ~2.88bn (2,880,471,000 at 2026-06-12), so the whole ~127m-share, 4.4%-of-shares-out supply is still to come and the Q1 10-Q filed with this print is its first disclosure window.
why_not_priced: The February plan was received as financing solved - CDS tightened sharply the day it was announced (CNBC, 2026-02-02) - and since then the $20bn ATM has only ever been referenced as an intention inside the FY2027 '$40bn of debt and equity' line, never as unexecuted supply. If the market were pricing 127m shares of imminent issuance into this print you would not see a -7.35 vol-point call-bid skew, a 0.79 put/call open-interest ratio and a 37% rally off the 24-July level of $114.99 (the price stamped in Oracle's own 2026-07-28 Form 4) with the stock closing the gap back to where the Vice Chairman sold in late June at $156-165. Equity issuance is the one mechanism that mechanically caps an up-tail, and a company that has just recovered 37% and must fund ~$90-95bn of gross FY2027 capex against $31.98bn of operating cash flow has both the motive and, as of 23 June, the expanded distribution machinery to sell into strength immediately after this print. This is a cluster: the R70 tag, the R8 cash flow line and the R1 share count are three readings of one document (the FY2026 10-K) and should count once; the 424B5 agent expansion is the genuinely separate leg.

Note it cuts mostly at FY2028 rather than FY2027, which is why the size is small.

Reformation's most recent full quarter before the pre-announced one, Q1 2026, was a GAAP NET LOSS of $12.1m, and its headline 70.3% gross margin was inflated by 904 basis points of a one-time IEEPA tariff refund recovering duties expensed in 2025 - so the entire 'profitable DTC' IPO narrative rests on a non-recurring credit, and the 10 September guide is the first time the company must show a margin without it.

If the market had this, the withdrawal of ~$27m of syndicate demand would have been written up somewhere and the stock's -4.46% five-day slide since 1 September would have a named cause; instead nothing at all was published. The conservative alternative allocation (shoe pro-rated at 15% of each holder's own sale) still gives only a 33% exercise and ~1.4m shares covered, so the finding survives either reading; I size on the conservative end.

text: The Q2 result itself carries essentially zero surprise capacity: the 424B4 pre-announced net revenue of $154.0-155.0m, gross profit $102.6-103.4m, net income $11.726-11.999m and adjusted EBITDA $24.9-25.3m for the thirteen weeks ended 2026-06-27 - a range one million dollars wide on $154m - so the classic first-post-IPO 'blowout beat' pop is arithmetically unavailable and the entire move is the first-ever Q3/FY guide.

If that asymmetry were priced you would not see a $19.25 consensus target set on 2026-08-24 sitting 43% above spot; the sell-side is still underwriting a re-rate that only a guide can deliver. Also note the pre-announced range implies +23.1% to +23.9% revenue growth against Q1 2026's +30.4% - a 6.5pt deceleration that the 'twenty consecutive quarters of double-digit growth' wire framing obscures.

text: Cutting the other way and genuinely material: 9,478,821 of the 14,062,500 IPO shares were PRIMARY, and the company is applying ~$125.1m of net proceeds to repay term loans that stood at $246.7m at 2026-06-27 - so interest expense roughly halves from Q3 onward, which is the single biggest driver of the gap between Q1's $15.9m adjusted EBITDA and its $(12.1)m net loss, and it means the first guided quarter's below-the-line is structurally better than any quarter in the historicals.

Combined with the permanent removal of the IEEPA tariff drag (which cost FY2025 364bp of gross margin), FY2026 adjusted EBITDA can be guided well above FY2025's $45.0m even with the refund stripped out, which is the plausible route to this print going the other way. Q4 FY25 is a freak comp that Q4 FY26 almost certainly cannot lap: last year's June quarter did $36.0m of gross profit on $227.8m of revenue at a 15.8% gross margin (vs 11.4% the prior year and 12.5% for FY25 as a whole) and $12.2m of adjusted EBITDA, whereas Q3 FY26's gross margin was 12.8% and DOWN 80bp YoY, so AENT needs roughly $281m of June-quarter revenue (+23.5% YoY) just to hold gross profit dollars flat.
why_not_priced: The 15.8% Q4 FY25 gross margin sits in a year-old press release and has never been flagged as non-recurring by anyone; if the market had done this arithmetic the three published targets (ThinkEquity, Maxim, Noble, median $10.33 against a $5.30 spot) would have been cut after the Q3 margin contraction on 2026-05-14, and they were not. text: The charter amendment intended to make AENT index-eligible was legally voided two weeks before this print: the Third Amended and Restated Certificate filed 2026-07-29 stripping Class E voting rights was nullified by a Certificate of Correction filed 2026-08-26 because it 'was not approved in compliance with the Second A&R Certificate', leaving the February 2023 charter operative — so the stated purpose in the July information statement (raising unrestricted float from 3.0% to 6.6% to clear Russell 3000's 5% threshold) has failed and must be redone.

A market that had read it would have marked down the index-inclusion optionality that the July information statement had just advertised, and would have asked about a four-week period of operating under an invalid charter.

text: The true tradeable float is far smaller than any data vendor shows: the DEF 14C states that as of 2026-06-24 only 3,371,581 Class A shares — 3.0% of the 110,979,630 total shares — were held by unrestricted shareholders, against a 20-day average volume of roughly 18,000 shares (~$96k) a day, so the earnings print is effectively the only liquidity window in the quarter for anyone wanting out.
why_not_priced: Screens report AENT's float as ~51m shares outstanding or ~11-25m 'float'; the company's own count of unrestricted holders is an order of magnitude smaller and appears only in an information statement mailed to holders in July. A market that knew the real float were 3.4m shares would not price this at a 14% typical print reaction — it would price it wider, and there is no options market pricing it at all.

text: RENT borrowed a $10,000,000 incremental term loan on 2026-09-01 'for working capital and other general corporate purposes' — ten days before the print and after the 2026-07-31 quarter end — even though the 10-Q states the minimum liquidity covenant was PERMANENTLY REMOVED by the First Amendment of 2026-01-28 and the Second Amendment of 2026-04-01 already lets it PIK interest until 2027-05-03; with no covenant to cure and no cash interest to service, the only reason left to take sponsor money is operating cash, which implies a Q2 cash balance far below the $37.1m at 2026-04-30 and the $43.6m at 2025-07-31.
why_not_priced: The 8-K is public and the stock has fallen, so the fact of the loan is partly in; what is not in is the arithmetic, which needs three documents read together. RENT burned $26.8m of cash in Q2 last year ($70.4m at 2025-04-30 to $43.6m at 2025-07-31); even at half that rate on the cut inventory plan, cash at 2026-07-31 lands near $20-27m against $157.1m of long-term debt and a $92m market cap. If the market had done that sum the stock would not need the print to find the number, and there would be a note somewhere stating a Q2 cash estimate — there is none, because the baseline notes this name is not well covered and there is no option chain to express it in.

text: On 2026-09-03 RENT signed a $9,000,000 Stipulation and Agreement of Settlement of the November 2022 IPO securities class action — $6m cash plus $3m in Class A stock, with insurers paying ~$2.9m and the company ~$3.1m — eight days before the print and five weeks after the 2026-07-31 balance sheet date, so under recognised-subsequent-event treatment the charge lands in the Q2 GAAP numbers being reported on 2026-09-11, and the stock component is ~1.1m new shares (~3.3%) on a 33.59m share count.
why_not_priced: The Q1 10-Q filed 2026-06-03 carried NO accrual for this case — it recited only the boilerplate that losses are accrued when probable and estimable — so any model built off the last filing has zero dollars in it for a charge that is now signed and quantified. The settlement was agreed after the quarter closed and after the earnings date was announced, so it cannot be in consensus by construction. If it were priced there would be a revised GAAP loss estimate in circulation; on a name with essentially one analyst there is not.

text: FY26 guidance cuts rental product acquired to $45-50m from $74.9m in FY25 — a ~35% reduction in the inventory that is the product — while ending Active Subscriber growth has already decelerated from ~+20% y/y in Q4 FY25 to +5.8% y/y in Q1 FY26 (155,692), and the dominant live customer complaint is that the assortment is empty ('tiny inventory with items rarely available for rent', 'items marked available now that aren't available in any size').

The Q2 comp is 146,373 actives, which last year fell sequentially from Q1, so a flat sequential quarter still prints ~+6% y/y and the headline metric looks fine — the damage shows up in the forward guide, which is the part no one has modelled. If the market had connected the capex cut to churn there would be a subscriber estimate below the +5.8% trend in circulation; the only public framing is 'revenue up 29%'.

RF Industries added brand-new deferred-tax-asset release language to its Q2 FY2026 10-Q MD&A that is absent from the Q1 10-Q filed three months earlier — 'it is reasonably possible that a reduction of a significant portion of the valuation allowance may be appropriate in a future reporting period', with 'cumulative losses' recast into the past tense ('In prior periods, the Company recorded a valuation allowance due primarily to cumulative losses') — against a $4,521,000 allowance which on 11,424,572 diluted shares is roughly $0.40 per share of potential one-time GAAP EPS, versus a $0.18 two-analyst consensus.
why_not_priced: This lives in the MD&A of a $110m microcap's 10-Q, not in the release, not in the 8-K exhibit and not on the call — and the comparison that makes it a signal requires pulling the prior quarter's 10-Q and diffing the tax paragraph. If it were priced there would be at least one sell-side or newswire note framing the Q3 print as a possible valuation-allowance quarter, and with only two analysts covering the name there is none; the consensus is a single clean $0.18 with no reconciliation between a GAAP and an ex-tax number, which is what you would not see if anyone had modelled a $0.40/share non-cash credit. The 'reasonably possible / future reporting period' construction is the standard ASC 740 pre-announcement companies file one to four quarters before they act, and Q3 (ended 31 July 2026) would be the fifth consecutive profitable quarter.

text: The -52% slide from the 16 July 2026 peak of $21.50 to $10.27 has no disclosed company-specific cause: EDGAR's full filing history for CIK 0000740664 shows the last 8-K of any kind was 2026-06-15, with nothing since except an ARS/DEF 14A on 2026-07-28, a routine 13G on 2026-07-29 and a 13G/A on 2026-08-14 — no S-3, no shelf takedown, no 424B, no prospectus supplement, and Form 4 activity only in the company's own recurring quarterly cluster (13 Jan, 14 Apr, 14 Jul).
why_not_priced: The sweep's own brief treats the -22.5% 20-day drawdown as the single most specific question on this name, which is how most participants will read it too: a halving into a confirmed date reads as the market discounting a bad quarter or an imminent raise. The filing record says the opposite — a $110m company that had actually lost a customer, drawn on a shelf, or seen management sell would normally leave a trace on EDGAR, and there is none. If the market were pricing a dilution risk you would expect at least an active S-3 takedown or a borrow build; if it were pricing a fundamental break you would expect an 8-K or a withdrawn guide. What is left is the unwind of a narrative re-rating (Russell 3000 inclusion 29 June, Zacks #1 on 23 July) rather than new information, which makes the reaction function into the print more symmetric than the drawdown implies.

text: COMEX copper ran at or near all-time highs through the whole of RF Industries' fiscal Q3 (1 May - 31 July 2026), printing a record $6.83/lb in August and sitting at $6.47/lb on 11 September, +41.2% over twelve months — against a business where custom cabling (37% of H1 FY2026 sales) plus interconnect (35%) is 72% of revenue and where the bar management set is a record 35.1% gross margin it called sustainable above $20m of quarterly revenue.
why_not_priced: Two analysts cover this name and the margin line they are modelling is the 35.1% management guided to as sustainable; nobody builds a copper pass-through lag into a $110m connector assembler. If input cost were in the price you would see a sell-side margin cut or at least a preview flagging it, and the only rating action in the window was a generic Zacks strong-buy-to-hold on 22 August. The mechanism is small but one-directional: RFIL buys finished cable, so a rising copper input shows up with a one-to-two-quarter lag precisely in the quarter being reported, and at roughly 15-25% of cabling COGS a 10% input move is worth about a point of gross margin, or ~$0.02 of EPS against a $0.18 bar.

text: The Middle East/Asia softness management called on 15 June 'not structural, it is a timing issue' that would 'resume swiftly' once pressure was alleviated instead escalated through the exact 1 May - 31 July fiscal Q3 window: the Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed to commercial traffic since 28 February 2026 and traffic slumped again in July on renewed US-Iran fighting and a blockade.
why_not_priced: Hormuz itself is the most heavily covered macro story of 2026 and is obviously priced as a macro fact. What is not priced is the specific link to this issuer: CODA's UAE/Gulf offshore-survey customers are the named cause of the Q2 Products shortfall, management publicly assumed alleviation, and the consensus above was never revised for the fact that the quarter being reported sat entirely inside the closure and got worse in its final month. If the market had made that link, the FY2026 revenue line would not still imply an H2 acceleration and the stock would not be flat over 20 days.

text: Coda Octopus has issued zero order or contract-award press releases in the sixteen months since 13 May 2025, against a prior cadence of three in ten weeks (a $1.3m engineering order 26-Mar-2025, a $1.4m engineering order 24-Apr-2025, a $1.5m DAVD order 13-May-2025) — and every one of its seven 2026 releases is an earnings or earnings-call item — despite the CEO telling investors on 15 June that 'we expect to see some orders in our third quarter' for DAVD following the Approved-for-Navy-Use designation.

If the market had priced a DAVD order failing to land, the Q2 call's single most-quoted forward statement would have been walked back somewhere in the coverage and the FY consensus cut; neither happened. Corroborated inside the Q2 10-Q, where customer concentration collapsed from three customers at 34.2% of H1 FY25 revenue to one customer at 10.2% of H1 FY26 — the large lumpy orders that generated those 2025 press releases have stopped arriving.

text: Inventory stood at $13,995,256 at 30 April 2026, up 2.6% from 31 October, against quarterly cost of revenue of about $2.33m — roughly 1.5 years of COGS — while the Marine Technology segment that carries it fell 19% in the half; and a brand-new CFO, Mark Kelly, started 3 August 2026, after the quarter closed, on a three-month probationary period, and signs his first 10-Q with this print.
why_not_priced: This is a conjunction nobody screens for: a first-time-signing CFO who arrived after quarter-end, replacing an interim, inheriting an inventory balance worth 1.5 years of cost of sales that is still growing into a shrinking high-margin segment. The 10-Q lands the same day as the release, so any reserve or obsolescence charge is disclosed simultaneously with the headline rather than a week later. If the market had focused on it there would be sell-side commentary on inventory turns or a CFO-transition note; CODA's coverage consists of one target-raise on 2026-06-17. Sized low as a mode because the modal outcome is that nothing happens, with a wide left tail.

The signed impact is positive but small because the shelf cuts the other way on a $111m market cap — a raise is the same event risk in reverse. If a deal were priced there would be a run-up rather than a 20-day drift of -1.18%.

text: Capital Markets - 37% of FY2025 revenue and gains ($73.1m) but 44% of segment EBITDA ($57.7m of $131.3m) - is the one line that cannot be reconstructed from the monthly AUM CoinShares publishes, and its largest single component was disclosed as ETH staking at $4.3m in Q2 2025 alone, a line that scales with token price and with a futures basis that compressed through a half in which industry ETP AUM fell from ~$160bn in May to ~$141bn by 1 June on record outflows.

If this were understood, the name would not be quoted on a trailing P/E at all and the 63% realised vol would already have an option chain around it rather than 368 total open interest.

High Tide carries a C$57.9m derivative liability for the put option over the 49% of Remexian it does not own, priced at 3.64065x Remexian's trailing annual EBITDA and valued by Monte Carlo with 82% annualised EBITDA volatility and a 15% IRR — so the liability ratchets up mechanically with exactly the record German quarter (10+ tonnes, +33% sequential) the company pre-announced, and the remeasurement lands below the three metrics the pre-announcement quantified.
why_not_priced: The Aug 4 pre-announcement quantified revenue, gross profit and adjusted EBITDA — the three measures that all exclude this item — and every wire story and preview ran on those three. The liability moved C$20.9m in its first two-month stub period in FY2025 against a Q2 FY2026 reported net income of C$24k, so a remeasurement of even a few million flips the reported bottom line to a loss against a quarter the company has already called a record. If the market had priced the mechanic, the Aug 4 release of record German tonnage would not have been a clean +4.65% up day, and the sell-side average target would not sit at $4.67 against a $2.57 spot with the put equal to roughly 19% of the US$221m market cap and settleable in cash or shares at High Tide's discretion from 2027-09-02.

text: The German MedCanG amendment that would ban mail-order dispensing and require in-person consultation before a first cannabis prescription was NOT voted before the 2026 summer recess and remains stuck in the Bundestag health committee over an unresolved coalition split on the scope of the mail-order ban, with a vote realistically no earlier than September 2026 and implementation drifting to late autumn/winter 2026.
why_not_priced: English-language cannabis coverage last framed this as 'Germany advances MedCanG amendments' and readers carried a spring-2026 enactment as the base case; the granular status — which committee, which coalition disagreement, which reading has not happened — exists only in German-language legal and trade sources. Remexian is a pharmacy wholesaler whose growth is fed by telemedicine-driven mail-order demand, so the delay is a direct extension of the runway that is under-reported in exactly the sources a cannabis analyst reads. If it were priced, the stock would not have traded to $2.15 on 2026-08-03, within 6% of its 52-week low, in the same week it pre-announced a record German quarter.

text: Free cash flow is the one metric the pre-announcement left out and it was already deteriorating before the German step-up: Q2 FY2026 FCF fell to C$1.5m from C$4.9m a year earlier on working-capital investment, TTM FCF is C$13.4m, cash was C$36.5m against C$68.2m of debt, and the company has publicly committed to staying FCF-positive for fiscal 2026 while Q3 revenue steps up C$16-21m sequentially on receivables-heavy German distribution plus a 20+ store build.

If the market had priced this, the slide would have come on a datable gap day with a news catalyst and there would be commentary attributing it; instead EDGAR full-text search returns no 6-K, no F-3, no 13D/A and no company filing of any kind between the 06-12 Q1 6-K and today, and no analyst action is findable. The second-order consequence is the part that matters tomorrow: the baseline hands the market a -43.67% run-up that reads as 'priced for disaster, primed to bounce', and the free control -run_up_20d_pct would rank COE among the day's strongest longs on that number alone — but the decline carries no fundamental information, so there is no disappointment discount to relieve, and no price-insensitive buyer left to absorb a soft print in a ~4m ADS float.
